solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Knowing about mediaeval instruments of torture jokes

parts.note: knowing, as in shrewd or sage, means wise
C is short for circa, Latin for about
the rack stretched its victims; racks are several of these devices

explanation.surface: A knowing remark about the torture devices of the Middle Ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knowing' looks like it describes someone, but it simply gives WISE; C stands for circa.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisecracks are smart, flippant quips, so they are a kind of joke.

clue.text: Promise news

definitions.meaning: to give your ... is to make a pledge

explanation.definitionFit: Word can mean a pledge (keep your word) and also tidings (send word).

clue.text: What a musician may do is express relief and walk

parts.note: a sigh is a breath let out in relief
to tread is to step or walk

explanation.surface: A musician breathes out in relief and strolls off.
explanation.definitionFit: Sight-reading is playing music at first sight from the score, a skill musicians practise.

clue.text: Density found in sort of rice beverage

indicators.note: the density symbol is placed within the shuffled grain word
a sort of rice is the letters of rice arranged differently

parts.note: D is the symbol for density in physics

explanation.surface: A drink made from some variety of rice, judged by its density.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges RICE into CIER, and 'found in' puts D inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cider is a fermented apple drink, so it is a beverage.

clue.text: Forbidding use at work with engineers

indicators.note: the two words are put to work, that is rearranged, as anagram material

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A stern ban on using something at work alongside engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at work' signals rearranging USE AT into AUSTE; the second 'at' is part of the fodder, not the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere and forbidding both describe a stern, severe, unwelcoming manner.

clue.text: Relations call back with regard to motion

parts.note: kin are one's relatives

indicators.note: back tells us the word for call is written right to left

parts.note: to cite is to summon or call, as a witness to court

explanation.surface: Family members return a phone call about some movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinetic means relating to or caused by movement, as in kinetic energy.

clue.text: Drug bill said to be cut by half

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

indicators.note: said is halved, its first two letters dropped

explanation.surface: A bill, it is said, is to be halved because of drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be cut by half' removes SA from SAID, leaving ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid is slang for the drug LSD.

clue.text: Policemen accept second of price cuts

indicators.note: the police word takes in a letter, accepting it inside

parts.note: cops is slang for police officers

indicators.note: second of points to the second letter of the word price

explanation.surface: The police agree to price reductions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second of' gives R from price, which 'accept' places inside COPS.
explanation.definitionFit: To crop is to trim or cut, so crops means cuts.

clue.text: Sporting knowledge?

parts.note: sporting reads as wearing clothes, so this is an understanding of what to wear, not of games

explanation.definitionFit: Dress sense is a feel for choosing clothes that suit you, a knowledge of what to sport.

clue.text: Standing to attention, free soldier inside

indicators.note: the soldier goes within the word for free

parts.note: to rid is to free or clear
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier standing to attention, longing to be free.
explanation.walkthrough: GI is the usual crossword soldier, from US army slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone standing to attention holds their body stiff, so rigid fits.

clue.text: Rock offering shade on beach

indicators.note: on places the shade word after the beach word in this across clue

parts.note: sands are a beach
a tone is a shade of colour

explanation.surface: A rock giving shade to people on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandstone is a sedimentary rock made of compacted sand grains.

clue.text: Runs in frightened, showing signs of injury

indicators.note: the runs letter goes in the word for frightened

parts.note: scared means frightened
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone runs in terrified, visibly hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarred skin bears the marks of old wounds, so it shows signs of injury.

clue.text: Rush for gold buried in river

indicators.note: the gold is buried, placed inside the river name

parts.note: the Trent is a major river in the English Midlands
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A rush to find gold buried in a riverbed.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic word for gold; the TRENT is an English river.
explanation.definitionFit: A torrent is a violent rush of water.

clue.text: Girls losing head become such animals

indicators.note: the girls word loses its first letter

parts.note: lasses are girls, especially in northern England and Scotland

explanation.surface: Girls who lose their heads end up making fools of themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'become' links wordplay to definition; 'such animals' refers back to what the wordplay makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Asses are donkeys, the animals named; the word also suggests fools.

clue.text: A peace trip planned to grow in value

indicators.note: a planned trip is one arranged, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A peaceful trip is arranged so that it will gain in value.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets that appreciate rise in worth over time.

clue.text: Childish pauses oddly cause annoyance

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of pauses

parts.note: to rile is to irritate

explanation.surface: Childish pauses can be strangely annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of pauses, PUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Puerile means childishly silly, from Latin puer, boy.

clue.text: Single charge put on empty lorry in anger

indicators.note: in a down clue, the charge sits on top of what follows

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a rate is a charge or fee

indicators.note: an empty lorry keeps only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone angrily pays a one-off fee for an empty lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' removes the inside of lorry, leaving LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Irately means angrily, so it stands for in anger.

clue.text: Flowers droop in centre

indicators.note: the droop word goes in the centre word

parts.note: the core is the centre
to sag is to droop

explanation.surface: Flowers drooping in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsage is a small spray of flowers worn on a dress.

clue.text: What's permitted when we call on a criminal?

indicators.note: a criminal version of the words is a crooked, rearranged one

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about how much is allowed when we visit an offender.
explanation.definitionFit: An allowance is an amount permitted, so it is what is permitted.

clue.text: About faces and calls again

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a dial is the face of a clock or watch

explanation.surface: Someone turns round and phones back.
explanation.definitionFit: To redial is to phone a number once more.

clue.text: Stay for day in Paris, accommodated by son

indicators.note: the son houses the day, holding it inside

parts.note: taken as written
jour is French for day

explanation.surface: A son puts someone up for a day's stay in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A sojourn is a temporary stay somewhere.

clue.text: Puzzles full of holes?

definitions.meaning: something riddled is pierced all over, as with bullets

explanation.definitionFit: Riddles are conundrums, and to riddle something is to pierce it with many holes.

clue.text: A dollop of Maori cottage cheese

indicators.note: a dollop is a portion, here a run of letters taken from inside the two words

explanation.surface: A spoonful of Maori cottage cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across MaoRI COTTAge.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft Italian whey cheese.

clue.text: Telegraph's lead?

parts.note: reads like the newspaper's top story, but means the wire that carries telegraph signals, and a telegram itself

explanation.definitionFit: A cable is both a telegram and an electrical lead or wire.

clue.text: Bush oddly accepted depression from strikes

indicators.note: the odd letters of the bush take in the depression
oddly takes the 1st and 3rd letters of Bush

parts.note: a low is a weather depression

explanation.surface: Bush strangely took depressing hits from strikes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' and 'accepted' are both indicators; a weather low is a depression, not a mood here.
explanation.definitionFit: Blows are hits or strikes.

clue.text: Thieving flyer's card and roll of cash returned

parts.note: a jack is a court card

indicators.note: the cash word is sent back, written right to left

parts.note: a wad is a roll of banknotes

explanation.surface: A thief has a playing card and gives back a roll of notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns WAD into DAW; the 's of the definition stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: The jackdaw is a crow famed for stealing shiny objects.

clue.text: Source of goodness in terrible song

indicators.note: the first letter of goodness goes in the word for terrible

parts.note: dire means terrible

indicators.note: source means where it starts, the first letter of goodness

explanation.surface: A song so awful it barely contains a shred of goodness.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a mournful song, as at a funeral.

clue.text: Go and get fired

definitions.meaning: a go is an attempt or try
a gun that has fired has been discharged

explanation.definitionFit: A shot is an attempt, and shot is the past form of fire a gun.

clue.text: Columnist shot in a city in front of relative

indicators.note: the first part is placed ahead of the relative
the shot word goes in the joined pieces a and city

parts.note: NY is New York
a go is a shot or attempt
an aunt is a relative

explanation.surface: A journalist is shot in a city in front of a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' looks like a gunshot but means a try; 'in' and 'in front of' are both indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: An agony aunt writes a newspaper advice column on readers' problems.

clue.text: Organised church spread

parts.note: to run an event is to organise it; ran is its past

explanation.surface: A church organised a buffet spread.
explanation.definitionFit: A spread is a large farm or estate, especially in the American West.

clue.text: Letters read out loud provide comfort

indicators.note: the letters are said aloud, giving the sound of a different word

parts.note: the letters are Es, more than one of the letter E

explanation.surface: Reading letters aloud brings comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease is to relieve or comfort.

clue.text: Fighting that might lead to union?

definitions.meaning: a betrothal leads to the union of marriage

explanation.definitionFit: An engagement is a battle, and a formal promise to marry, which leads to wedlock.
